commit 51a9a21bb3e27511ab293bc5b09b6b20d329f26c
ordinal 96
date 2026-08-07 23:41:27 -0700
author Matt Stults
subject Adversarial spec-drift review: 8 confirmed drifts, 5 suspected
Clean-context review of today's stage-3/stage-4 build against
resources/03_pipeline.md, STEP_stage3.md and STEP_stage4.md rev 2.

The three that matter:

A1 The `_` guard in `_check_body` was withdrawn on a renderer ground.
   The design's ground was never the renderer -- 03_pipeline.md:33 names
   XCLINGO, and STEP_stage4.md:224 makes xclingo load-bearing for R3.
   Ran it: xclingo 2.0b24 still crashes on `p(X) :- q(X,_).`, control
   without `_` is clean. Failure mode 7 is re-opened, loud, and it takes
   the whole link set's explanation down. Restore the guard on the
   xclingo ground. (The `_check_term` half, kept for rule HEADS, is
   correctly regrounded -- only the body half is wrong.)

A2 `probe.impossible_findings` builds a `probe-structural` finding --
   disclosable -- out of a SEAT LABEL, naming the situation and its
   atoms, and it reaches a stage-1 repair prompt. Reproduced. The
   design's own grounds sentence for that origin ("no expected verdict
   anywhere near them") is false of it.

A3 RB1's act-term exemption exists ONLY in readback.py. STEP_stage4.md
   :415 grants exactly one exception, the clause reference; rev 2 did
   not amend 2.4. 19 of 19 `asserts` renderings in runs/ show a bare
   functor. Asked for a view: it is a hole in Invariant 1, not an
   implementation limit -- it covers the deontic head of every rule and
   re-imports ASP2CNL's naming model that 2.3a rejects by name.

Also: RB4 is structurally blind to layer-1 content (rev 2 DID weaken a
check while saying it did not); `readback.Finding` has no `origin` so
`readback-structural` cannot be registered as 5.5 requires in the same
diff; the layer-1 fraction is required in the report and absent; the
stage-3 seat's "and any behaviour" denial is unenforced and `b_asserts(`
slips `\basserts\s*\(` on a word boundary.

One where the CODE is right and the DESIGN is stale: 8's mutation bar
for stage 4 cannot be met by mutate_schema.py, which deletes ast.Raise
nodes -- readback.py has zero, by design. Ran the substitute battery by
hand instead: RB1-RB5 and the ungloss check are all genuinely pinned.

Review only. No code, test or design document changed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

----END----

commit 9bb82bc0fe2444885c19aeabef8025cfab4586fe
ordinal 97
date 2026-08-07 23:44:58 -0700
author Matt Stults
subject Adversarial review of today's stage-3/4 work: 12 findings, 2 high
Clean-context review of f775bc2..HEAD. Review only -- no code, test or
document outside this file changed; every verification mutation restored.

The two that matter:

* `_parse_body` silently drops everything after the first statement in a
  body. `_check_body` rejects only a TRAILING full stop, so
  `adult(P). N > 5, N != 9` validates, and the seats are shown a sentence
  carrying one of its three conditions -- with RB1-RB5 all green and zero
  findings. RB2 only scans `name(` so a dropped comparison is invisible to
  it, and RB3 computes `want` and `got` from the same truncated parse, so it
  agrees with itself. A drop, not a refusal -- which is why totality held
  everywhere else I attacked it.

* `test_an_anonymous_variable_in_a_BODY_is_accepted_and_clingo_loads_it`
  passes when clingo never ran: no returncode check, and "No module named
  clingo" contains no `error`. It is the entire positive evidence for
  withdrawing the `_check_body` guard, and it was written in the same commit
  series that fixed exactly this shape in `link._check_clingo`.

Also: `translate.py --self-test` has been RED (51/1, exit 1) through all four
commits while pytest read 468 green, because the pytest wrapper asserts only
"did not crash"; `REVIEW_QUEUE.md`'s "WHAT IS BUILT AND GREEN" still claims
53/53, 270 tests, 45 guards (actual 51+1 failed, 468, 44).

Re-ran both sweeps rather than trusting them: mutate_schema 44/44 killed,
and 12 of 15 hand-written readback mutants killed, each by exactly one
targeted test. The three survivors are findings F6 and F7. The pin set is
real work; these are its edges.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

----END----

commit b7c663e056a2d1f5b050d71d067773e6fea496a5
ordinal 98
date 2026-08-07 23:47:48 -0700
author Matt Stults
subject RESTORE the anonymous-variable guard: I withdrew it on the wrong tool
The spec-drift review caught this and it is my error. I briefed the withdrawal
as "the ground is disproved twice over", citing bare clingo (which does derive
from `p(X) :- q(X,_)`) and the published ASP2CNL renderer (which skips hidden
terms). Both claims are TRUE and both are about the wrong tool.

03_pipeline.md names XCLINGO, and STEP_stage4.md makes it load-bearing for
stage 4's R3 derivation layer. [RAN] xclingo 2.0b24:

  p(X) :- q(X,_).  ->  error: unsafe variables in:
                         _xclingo_sup(2,0,p(X),(#Anon0,X)):-...
  p(X) :- q(X,Y).  ->  |__"p holds of a"

xclingo lifts body variables into a supporting term where an anonymous one
becomes unsafe. It is not a limitation we can render around, and it takes the
WHOLE LINK SET's explanation down, not one rule. 03_pipeline.md:239 stage-2
node D1 still requires "no anonymous placeholders" -- the code now matches the
design again.

THE REPLACEMENT TEST RUNS XCLINGO rather than asserting the validator
complains. That is the whole difference: the old test checked only that
something raised, which is exactly what let the guard be withdrawn on a false
premise. The new one pins the GROUND, with a named-variable control proving the
failure is caused by the `_` and not by the fixture, and it refuses to pass
quietly if xclingo is missing.

test_readback keeps `_` in its direct-rendering list and excludes it from the
module-level one. The split is the point: the renderer must handle `_` (the
hand-written .lp files contain it) while the contract refuses to emit it.
Conflating "renderable" with "admissible" is what caused this.

Lesson, recorded because it cost a wrong commit: "the renderer can handle it"
is not a claim about renderers in general. Name the tool and run it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

----END----

commit f8f83edb52cf88551b3cb37ea44bf6e05e240aeb
ordinal 99
date 2026-08-07 23:52:17 -0700
author Matt Stults
subject Close the silent content drop: an internal full stop hid two thirds of a rule
Engineering review F1, HIGH, and it is the worst class of defect this project
has -- not a refusal, a DROP.

schema._check_body rejected only a TRAILING full stop, so
`adult(P). N > 5, N != 9` validated. readback._parse_body wrapped it, clingo
parsed TWO statements, and the loop returned the first Rule's literals and
discarded the rest. A seat was shown one of three conditions with
outcome=rendered, RB1-RB5 all True and zero findings.

Neither backstop could reach it. RB2 scans for `name(`, and a dropped
comparison has none. RB3 counts `not` in the same broken parse on both sides,
so it agrees with itself. That is why layer-1 totality held everywhere else and
this still got through.

Fixed at BOTH layers. The contract now rejects a statement separator in a body,
with `1..3` preserved -- the interval operator is legal and a naive guard bans
it, so that control is a test. The renderer refuses to return a partial parse
and falls back to layer 1 over the RAW text instead, so nothing is lost and the
report shows it as ASP-with-glosses rather than fluent English. Defence in
depth is deliberate: trusting the layer above is how the first one got through.

RED-verified both ways. 471 tests, mutate_schema 0 survivors.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

----END----

RB1 act exemption (same root as Q-7), RB4 blind to layer-1 content, no origin

commit 29e018c6dcf7a530c1f53ec1b64a2a6ed3b6b1d7
ordinal 101
date 2026-08-08 00:04:05 -0700
author Matt Stults
subject stage 4: the four review seats, enforced rather than stated
`STEP_stage4.md` §§4–6. `readback.py` composes the one artifact all four seats
judge; `seats.py` decides who is shown what, computes the four denominators,
adjudicates the replies, and writes a report in which four agreeing seats
cannot read as confirmation.

§4's three shared reasons, each answered structurally:

  A they all read the same rendering — `build_4c_prompt` has NO PARAMETER a
    rendering could arrive through, and renderer marks smuggled through the
    item text are refused. 4c is the anchor because it is not downstream of 4r.
  B the rendering echoes the clause — RB4's stamp: 4b/4d verdicts marked
    `non-evidential`, still asked, still recorded, never counted.
  C unanimity read as confirmation — no consensus field, no `n_passed`, no
    pass fraction, refused at construction; 4a in `advisory` and the pass line
    provably does not read it; 4d `covered` cross-checked against stage 3's
    discrimination count, `unsupported` where that number does not exist.

The four denominators (§5.1) and what each excludes: 4a the rendered set; 4b
minus `world`; 4c every licensed item WITH `concepts` (excluding them takes the
run's denominator 12 -> 1); 4d the claims list minus `forbid_body` claims,
excluded by name and reported separately so a clause whose only gap is one
cannot read as full coverage.

Leak perimeter (§5.5/§5.6): `readback-structural` disclosable, every seat
origin and `covered-but-inert` not; a seat finding discards the transcript and
re-translates from a clean prompt, carrying zero bits.

TDD, RED first. 134 tests, every fence with a paired silent control. Mutation
sweep `mutate_seats.py`: 83 mutants, 0 survivors — the first run had 16
survivors out of 71 with all 103 tests green, and each is now named.

Three defects found reviewing this against DEBUGGING_TIPS §8, all the same
shape (a check that did not run reading like one that passed): RB4 with no
clause quote reported every verdict as evidential; RB1/RB2/RB3 fire without
changing the read-back outcome, so a rendering with a surviving label reached a
seat unmarked; and a stamped negative verdict lost its stamps on the way into
the finding. All three now stamp — on RB4's precedent, never a gate.

⛔ NOTHING WAS SPENT. `judge` raises without an explicit `client_factory` and
every seat is exercised against stubs. Measured cost of a live run, off the
artifact that actually renders (`seats.py --cost`, free): 7 of 19 stored
modules reach a seat, worst case $0.0051/clause at flash rates and
$0.5111/clause at frontier.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

----END----

commit 0defdbc45bcf2cb3a6db187a7cea1cea055c807f
ordinal 102
date 2026-08-08 00:07:06 -0700
author Matt Stults
subject Q-3 answered with a measured number; two gaps recorded
A full stage-4 run over everything that can reach a seat costs about FOUR CENTS
on the configured flash model (worst case, every reply at its token cap). On a
frontier model it is $3.58 -- 42% of the remaining project budget. Computed by
seats.py --cost from the real rendered artifact, no calls made.

Only 7 of 19 stored modules reach a seat: 5 fail stage 2, 7 are blocked by
readback-ungloss. The check was not relaxed to raise that number.

Q-16: stage 4 section 2.1 specifies THREE rendering layers and readback.py
produces two. R3, the xclingo derivation trees, is absent -- no derivation
reaches any seat and the seats judge items and rules but never why a verdict
followed. Unfinished implementation rather than a design question, so I am
building it.

Q-17: 4c never runs for the 7 ungloss-blocked modules, so the seat designed to
be independent of the shared artifact is switched off exactly when that artifact
fails. Independent of a WRONG rendering, not of a MISSING one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

----END----
